schema.description:
roleType is optional. A predefined roleType must be supplied without nonempty
permissions; an omitted or empty array is accepted.
CUSTOM requires a nonempty permissions array. When roleType is omitted, a nonempty
permissions array is an explicit CUSTOM grant: legacy WRITE grants write operations
only and is not converted to the predefined WRITE role, which also grants read and
delete operations. If neither field is supplied, or permissions is empty with no
roleType, the legacy READ, WRITE and DELETE defaults apply. Unknown role types or
permission names, and invalid field combinations, are rejected. ADMIN roles and ADMIN
permission grants are not allowed, even for administrators.

groups.description: Optional list of groups to add as custom claims to API Key

customClaims.description:
Optional custom application claims to associate with the API key. Values may be
strings, numbers, Booleans, arrays, or objects and retain their JSON types.
Null-valued object fields are omitted.
Claims are exposed through userClaims when authenticating with this key and do not
override its username, site, groups, role, or permissions. Omission means no custom
claims.

roleType.description:
A predefined permission role or CUSTOM for selecting individual permissions.
ADMIN grants all scoped permissions. GOVERN grants governance, read, write and
delete permissions outside the dedicated management roles. WRITE also grants
read and delete permissions. SYSTEM_MANAGEMENT and USER_MANAGEMENT grant their
respective management permissions. READ and DELETE grant their matching
operation permissions. CUSTOM has no implicit grants.
roleType.title: ApiPermissionRoleType

permissions.description:
Explicit scoped or legacy umbrella grants for CUSTOM or an omitted roleType.
Required and nonempty when roleType is CUSTOM. For predefined role types,
omit this field or supply an empty array.
Legacy requests without roleType keep the default grants when this is empty.

items.description:
An explicit permission grant. Scoped names match those returned by the permission
catalog. The legacy ADMIN, DELETE, READ, WRITE and GOVERN umbrella names are also
accepted for compatibility. These names are explicit grants, not selections of a
predefined role type; for example, WRITE alone does not imply READ or DELETE.
RetentionPolicy and ReminderPolicy in the PRESET namespace require their dedicated
policy grants in place of READ_ENTITY, WRITE_ENTITY and DELETE_ENTITY.
Use roleType to select a predefined role. Administrator grants require an
administrator caller.
items.title: ApiPermissionGrant
